name: Wat
description: A human squire barely more than a boy -- sixteen or seventeen -- low-born, with a stable-yard name and stable-yard beginnings. Green, eager, and idealistic, he hero-worships Ser Warrant openly and without guile. Quick, willing, and so young that his faith has never once been tested.
backstory: Low-born like the knight he serves -- which is very likely why Tomas took him on, and why Tomas trusted him as he trusts no one else. Wat is the one person alive to whom the knight has given his true name and the truth of his bonded origins; the boy guards it as a sacred thing and worships his master the more for it, seeing in Tomas's rise the proof that the oath can raise a nobody to greatness. He believes in the oath, in the kingdom, and in Ser Warrant with an idealist's whole and undivided heart. When the Emberkin bargain is struck and Tomas stays behind as guarantor, it is Wat the knight sends riding home with the caravan to fetch the crown's resources -- the faithful errand that will, all unknowing, become the blade that ends his master's love.
motivation: WANT: to prove himself worthy of Ser Warrant, to carry out his charge faultlessly, and to become a knight like his hero. NEED (arc): to learn that his hero is a man and not a legend -- that the oath he idealizes can cost a soul everything -- and to grow, too soon, from the boy who admires into someone who understands.
arc: The green idealist whose loyal errand is the unwitting blade. He returns not with triumph but with alarm: a summons that the two empires are sliding toward war and the buffer-kingdom needs its guarantor home -- so that Tomas's return now carries not just his oath but his whole people's survival. Finding his master changed among the Emberkin, Wat cannot let himself see it: he clings to the mission and to 'we can go home now, Ser,' his love and his innocence blinding him, and in that blindness he becomes one more gentle force steering Tomas back toward duty. Whatever he finally understands of his master's choice is the end of his boyhood.
traits: believes wholly in the oath and his master
willfully blind to what he cannot bear to see

relationships.Tomas (Ser Warrant): His master and hero -- and the man who trusted him alone with the truth of his name and birth. Wat's devotion, and the faithful errand he rides, are tragically part of what pulls and forces Tomas away from Soraya; on his return he innocently urges his hero homeward, unable to see the love in front of him.
relationships.Soraya and the Emberkin: He rides off before the romance takes root and returns to find his master among the 'cursed' folk -- and refuses to see what it is, clinging to the mission and the road home.
relationships.The kingdom / court: The conduit through which the war-summons reaches Tomas -- the boy who carries his nation's need on his shoulders without grasping what answering it will cost the man he loves.

theSummons: On the road home Wat learns, and carries back, that the two empires the kingdom brokers between are sliding toward war; the fragile peace frays and the crown needs its guarantors, Tomas foremost. Return is thus no longer only about the oath -- it is about whether the buffer-kingdom survives at all.
openQuestions: How much Wat comes to understand by the end; whether the war actually breaks (within the book's frame or beyond it); his eventual fate -- knighted and haunted, or disillusioned of the oath he worshipped.
